extracted.intended_audience: secondary (high school) STEM educators and STEM education researchers
extracted.subtask_description: A conceptual framework and practical guidance for designing, implementing, researching, and evaluating integrated STEM education at the secondary (high school) level, emphasizing situated learning, STEM practices, and teacher professional development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of integrated STEM education
rubrics_metrics.description: Integrated STEM education is defined as the approach to teaching the STEM content of two or more STEM domains, bound by STEM practices within an authentic context for the purpose of connecting these subjects to enhance student learning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operationalization notes: integration may occur in a class/unit/lesson based on connections and real-world problems; curriculum models can be focused on one subject with contexts from others; authors acknowledge limits (some theoretical content may not afford design-based instruction).

rubrics_metrics.name: Situated STEM learning (contextualization)
rubrics_metrics.description: STEM content should be grounded in situated cognition: learning contexts (physical and social) are critical; understanding how knowledge/skills are applied is as important as acquiring them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use authentic contexts (e.g., engineering design) to make learning relevant and transferable. Anti-patterns/limits: some STEM content cannot be situated; the situated-as-load metaphor may be limited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engineering design as the integrator
rubrics_metrics.description: Use engineering design as a primary integrative approach—provides systematic problem-solving, authentic context, and an entry point to include engineering practices across STEM.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engineering design supports use of science inquiry and mathematical reasoning, allows modeling and prototyping, leverages reasoning under uncertainty. Limitations: not all science/math topics can be taught via design; design and inquiry converge but are distinct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific inquiry practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt inquiry-based instruction that encourages and models skills of scientific inquiry (questioning, hypothesizing, investigating) and cultivates curiosity, openness, and skepticism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: True inquiry requires 'minds-on' constructivist approaches rather than merely hands-on tasks. Teachers need authentic research/inquiry experiences and strengthened pedagogical content knowledge to implement real inquiry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technological literacy (the 'T' in STEM)
rubrics_metrics.description: Teach technology beyond tool use: as bodies of knowledge, activities, artifacts, and volition; include both engineering/instrumental and humanities/value-laden perspectives of technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate Standards for Technological Literacy (ITEA/STL), explore technology's socio-cultural, economic, political, and environmental impacts, and consider teaching engineering and technology jointly (Engineering Technology Education). Avoid reducing 'T' to mere educational tech.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematical thinking and modeling
rubrics_metrics.description: Embed mathematical thinking (modeling, abstraction, quantitative reasoning) within authentic STEM contexts so students see relevance and can use math to evaluate design solutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage Common Core math practice standards (e.g., make sense of problems, reason abstractly, model with mathematics). Note limits: some math content may not map to design problems; student cognitive development can constrain applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community of practice (social rope)
rubrics_metrics.description: Frame integrated STEM learning within communities of practice where novices participate alongside experienced practitioners to develop shared practices and move toward mastery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use partnerships with scientists, engineers, technologists, industry; promote shared practices, observation, discussion, and participation. Challenges: teachers must network and allow external participants into classrooms; some students may struggle in social learning environments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teach content alongside STEM practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Learning outcomes should include both domain content and the disciplinary practices (science, engineering, technology, mathematics) to reveal similarities/differences and facilitate transfer across domains.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use explicit comparison of science vs engineering practices (see table of practice comparisons) and select key practices from each domain to ground outcomes. Emphasize that practices and content are equally important.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design and implementation quality criteria for integrated STEM
rubrics_metrics.description: High-quality integrated STEM programs should intentionally integrate technology and engineering into science and mathematics, promote inquiry, rigorous mathematics and engineering design, and connect learners with STEM professionals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Kennedy & Odell recommended components: (a) integrate tech/engineering into science and math at minimum; (b) promote inquiry plus rigorous math/engineering/science instruction; (c) collaborative approaches linking students/educators to professionals; (d) global/multi-perspective views; (e) project-based and formal/informal experiences; (f) appropriate technologies to enhance learning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teacher knowledge and professional development
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective integrated STEM teaching requires teachers' sufficient content knowledge and pedagogical content knowledge plus professional development to build conceptual understanding and confidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide PD with authentic inquiry/design experiences, scientist–teacher partnerships, and sustained community-of-practice supports. PD should aim to increase teacher self-efficacy for integrated STEM instruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research and evaluation agenda criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Research on integrated STEM must document interventions in detail (how integration is enacted and supported), identify clear outcomes, and measure impacts on learning, thinking, interest, identity, and equity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Researchers should report nature of integration, scaffolding, instructional designs; use design experiments and longitudinal studies; address diversity and equity; measure teacher and student identity, interest, self-efficacy, and content learning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program goals and measurable outcomes (example: TRAILS)
rubrics_metrics.description: Program-level goals and measurable outcomes should be explicit (example TRAILS goals: teacher PD for STEM knowledge/practices; sustainable communities of practice; engage grades 9–12 learners via engineering design and 3D tech; strategies for underserved/rural students).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggested measures include: (a) teacher self-efficacy for integrated STEM teaching; (b) awareness of STEM careers among students and teachers; (c) students' use of 21st-century skills in engineering design; (d) student growth in STEM career interest, self-efficacy, and content knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize limits and constraints of integration
rubrics_metrics.description: Be explicit about limits: not all STEM topics can be integrated via design or situated contexts; integration could constrain coverage of necessary theoretical knowledge; student cognitive development and assessment structures (e.g., departmental silos, exams) may limit implementation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan for selective integration where appropriate, supplement with theoretical instruction when needed, and anticipate systemic barriers (standards, assessments, departmental agendas) that can hamper integrated approaches.
